clue.text: Ban for bomb with which I take part

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
H as in H-bomb, the hydrogen bomb
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: Someone joins a protest movement to ban the bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with which' and 'take' are link words; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit is to forbid something officially, a synonym of ban as a verb.

clue.text: New lamps in service

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Fresh lamps are installed for a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song sung during a church service, so it is part of worship.

clue.text: One employed as a killer in the main

definitions.text: One employed as a killer in the main

parts.words: One employed as a killer in the main
parts.note: the main is the old poetic word for the open sea; the clue reads like a hired assassin who is mostly a killer

explanation.surface: Someone whose job is, for the most part, killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly', but it means at sea, where whales are hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaler who throws the barbed spear at whales works as a killer out at sea.

clue.text: Top style obtained at a place bustling with activity

definitions.meaning: a tall domed hairstyle of the 1960s, a style for the top of the head
a busy place, likened to a home of swarming bees

explanation.surface: A fashionable hairdo was acquired at a busy salon.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a towering bouffant hairdo and, figuratively, any busy, crowded place full of workers.

clue.text: Like two nudists who were completely incompatible?

definitions.text: Like two nudists who were completely incompatible?

parts.words: Like two nudists who were completely incompatible?
parts.note: read literally, nudists are entirely without suits of clothes, while the phrase also means utterly ill-matched

explanation.surface: A naturist couple who just did not get on.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means utterly ill-matched, and literally describes people wholly without suits of clothing.

clue.text: Brave place to live

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, so this is his dwelling, not a courageous home

explanation.surface: A daring place to set up home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A domed tent-like hut is the traditional dwelling of some Native American peoples.

clue.text: Fly before end of summer, bird

indicators.note: the fly comes before, so it is placed first in the answer

parts.note: the warble fly is a fly whose larvae live under cattle hides

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of summer

explanation.surface: A fly appears before summer ends, along with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A warbler is a small songbird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Union ceremony

definitions.meaning: a marriage, the joining of two people
the formal service at which a couple are married

explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is both a union of two people and the ritual occasion where they are joined.

clue.text: It is compulsory for fellow attorney, a right-winger

parts.note: a fellow is a man
DA is the abbreviation for district attorney, a US prosecutor
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, on the right

explanation.surface: An obligation imposed on a lawyer who happens to be a conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mandatory is required by rule, a synonym of compulsory.

clue.text: States egghead is unwilling

parts.note: avers means declares or states
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: Someone declares that an intellectual is reluctant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it gives the head (first letter) of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being reluctant or opposed, a synonym of unwilling.

clue.text: Excited? No

parts.note: the clue word No is what you get when the word on is turned round

explanation.surface: Was someone thrilled? Not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, 'turned ON', and it produces the clue word No.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aroused or stimulated is a common slang sense of excited.

clue.text: Stonemason's unforgettable work?

parts.note: not a brilliant piece of craft but a carved stone made so that someone is not forgotten

explanation.surface: Praise for a stonemason's most memorable creation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unforgettable' seems to mean outstanding; it means made to keep someone in memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument carved in stone commemorates the dead so they are remembered.

clue.text: Beast went back to the plate

indicators.note: went back says the word for beast is read from end to start

parts.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal retreated to its dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went back' reverses ANIMAL; 'to the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin layer or flat plate, as of metal or bone.

clue.text: Opportunity of taking public transport to court

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone gets the chance of a bus or train to reach court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of taking' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is a division of the English High Court, a court of equity.

clue.text: Painstaking building supervisor?

parts.note: split differently, someone who takes care, that is painstaking, looks after a building

explanation.surface: A meticulous person in charge of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor looks after a building; split in two, the word is one who takes care.

clue.text: Soldier taken in by repulsive ogre in Italian port

indicators.note: taken in by means the soldier is placed inside the other letters
repulsive here works as driven back and jumbled, so the word ogre is rearranged

parts.note: GI is the usual word for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is captured by a hideous monster in an Italian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsive' rearranges the monster's letters to REGO, and 'taken in by' places the American soldier inside them, before the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: Reggio di Calabria is a seaport at the toe of Italy.

clue.text: Big hit that's a tricky achievement

definitions.meaning: in baseball, a home run with all bases loaded
winning all the major tournaments in tennis or golf, or all tricks in bridge

explanation.surface: A huge strike that is hard to pull off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' hints at bridge, where taking every trick is the feat.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers a bases-loaded home run in baseball and a clean sweep of every major title or every bridge trick.

clue.text: Inflexible person gets the stick

definitions.meaning: a rod for ramming the charge into an old gun or cleaning its barrel

explanation.surface: A rigid person gets beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a straight rod used with muzzle-loading guns and, figuratively, a stiff, unbending person.

clue.text: Lady left at home feeling weakly sentimental

parts.note: Maud is a woman's name
in means at home

explanation.surface: A woman left alone at home feels mawkish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeling' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means tearfully, self-pityingly emotional, a synonym of weakly sentimental.

clue.text: Man getting a duck in both innings will give up

parts.note: Des is a man's name
in cricket a pair is being out for no score (a duck) in both innings of a match

explanation.surface: A batsman scoring nothing twice will lose heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'will' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, a sense of give up.

clue.text: No redhead, Amanda, found in France

parts.note: the head of red is its first letter, R
Mandy is a pet form of Amanda

explanation.surface: Amanda is not a redhead, says someone who met her in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link word; the definition is a region in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy is a region of northern France.

clue.text: Thief turning over a new F leaf?

definitions.text: Thief turning over a new F leaf?

parts.words: Thief turning over a new F leaf?
parts.note: not a reformed criminal but one whose leaves make a crackling sound, rustling

explanation.surface: A criminal who decides to reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over a new leaf' suggests reform, but a stealer of cattle who makes leaves crackle is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief is a rustler, and to rustle is also to make dry leaves crackle.

clue.text: Bull, he's taken out of the dictionary

indicators.note: taken out of means those letters are removed from the word for dictionary

parts.note: a thesaurus is a dictionary of synonyms
taken as written, the letters h-e-s

explanation.surface: A bull's entry has been removed from the dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out of' removes HES from THESAURUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus is the zodiac sign and constellation of the bull.

clue.text: Rough land used to dislodge one from a horse

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Rough ground used to unseat a rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsaddle is to throw a rider, removing them from the horse's back.

clue.text: Animal getting into the landing-craft

indicators.note: getting into means the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A beast climbs aboard the landing-craft.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Unit of power or weight that which is said to follow

indicators.note: to follow puts the second piece after the weight

parts.note: kilo is short for kilogram, a weight

indicators.note: is said signals that the word for that which is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: what means that which

explanation.surface: A unit of power or weight, and that which is supposed to come next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilowatt is a thousand watts, a measure of electrical power.

clue.text: Dolores puts it in novel

indicators.note: in means the word it goes inside the name

parts.note: Lola is a pet form of Dolores

explanation.surface: Dolores includes it in her book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts' is a link. Fittingly, the heroine of Nabokov's novel is Dolores Haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is Vladimir Nabokov's 1955 novel.

clue.text: Guide dog

definitions.meaning: a senior member of the Girl Guides, or a park warden who shows visitors round
a hound that ranges widely in search of game

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a senior Girl Guide or park warden and an old name for a roving hunting dog.

clue.text: Dung-beetle Tim squeezed the middle out of, and in Germany that's where this is found

definitions.text: in Germany that's where this is found

parts.note: the dor is a dung-beetle

indicators.note: squeezed the middle out of means the central letter of the name is removed

parts.note: und is German for and

explanation.surface: A beetle squashes a man named Tim, somewhere in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezed the middle out of' removes I from TIM; UND is German for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dortmund is a city in western Germany, the place described.
